content:
The test image shows tomato leaves with extensive irregular brown necrosis, dry/papery texture, holes where tissue has fallen out, and yellow-green coloration on adjacent tissue. Affected part: **leaves**. Key features: large irregular brown necrotic patches, no obvious concentric rings, no white fuzzy growth visible.

Top candidates: Late Blight, Early Blight, Bacterial Canker, Septoria Leaf Blotch.

Now I'll view one reference from each of my top 4 candidates.
Late Blight reference matches well: large irregular brown necrotic patches, papery texture, similar to the test image. Now checking Early Blight.
Early Blight shows discrete dark lesions with concentric rings - doesn't match the extensive irregular necrosis in the test image. Checking Bacterial Canker.
Bacterial Canker shows marginal scorch and some spots - partial match but margins are more prominent than central necrosis in test image. Checking Septoria Leaf Blotch.

Septoria shows many small circular spots - completely different from the test image's large irregular necrotic patches.

**Summary of comparisons:**
- **Late Blight**: Best match - large irregular brown necrotic patches, papery/dry texture, similar pattern of tissue death spreading across leaves
- **Early Blight**: Doesn't match - discrete dark spots with concentric rings
- **Bacterial Canker**: Partial match - mainly marginal necrosis, different pattern
- **Septoria**: No match - small circular spots

The test image shows extensive, irregular brown necrosis covering large leaf areas with papery/dry texture and holes where tissue has collapsed - most consistent with Late Blight's characteristic large irregular brown lesions.
